posts.title: If I Had Died Then
posts.description: This Thanksgiving week, I am on the road again — not to some far-off remote location on the other side of the planet, but to the familiar place my heart calls home. My journey to my childhood home takes me past a particular spot marked indelibly on the map of my heart, a once brush-covered piece of geography next to what used to be a two-lane county road. It is the place where I almost lost my life forty-nine years ago. The events of that day in 1977 are still embedded on the front pages of my memory. It was a beautiful day as I cruised home from college in my old ’62 Chevy Malibu. In the distance, I noticed a car on the shoulder of the road. As I approached, the driver suddenly veered back onto the road to make a U-turn. The elderly driver did not see me. My foot never reached the brake pedal, and I had only a second to turn the steering wheel a tiny fraction to the left before impact. The impact was horrific. posts.title: A Fresh Look at the 10/40 Window
posts.description: In 1998, I traveled 26 hours by train from Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, to Beijing, China. As my train crossed the Gobi Desert, I read through the book of Acts. God used that train ride to speak to me about the direction of my life and ministry. On that journey, God convicted me about the plight of the world’s remaining unreached people groups. I knew I had to learn more about these peoples and how God might use me to move in their direction. I discovered that most of the world’s unreached peoples live in a region missiologists call the 10/40 Window. This region is defined by 10 and 40 degrees north latitude, stretching from North Africa to East Asia. The more I learned, the more convinced I became that I should invest as much of my life and energy as possible in raising awareness, raising funds, and mobilizing teams to come alongside those serving among the unreached in that region. posts.title: One More | Kingsland Missions 2027
posts.description: Every December, I look forward to sharing our annual missions report and vision for the year ahead with our Kingsland family. This year’s publication is titled ONE MORE , and I hope you will take a few moments to read it when it arrives in your mailbox. The title reflects something that has been on my heart for a long time. In the closing scenes of the movie Schindler’s List , Oskar Schindler reflects on the lives he helped save during the Holocaust. Rather than focusing on the more than 1,000 people he rescued, he is overcome with emotion as he considers what more he might have done. Looking at his possessions, he realizes that if he had sold them, he might have saved one more person. That scene has stayed with me because one more is a person with a name, a family, and a future. Since Kingsland officially launched our missions ministry in July 2005, God has allowed us to take the good news of Jesus to people in some of the world’s most difficult places.
